sections.skill: Explain property, life, and disability insurance and estimate coverage needs

questions.prompt: Which insurance replaces part of your paycheck if illness or injury keeps you from working?

choices.text: Life insurance, which pays when someone dies
Disability insurance
Homeowners insurance, which covers the house
Health insurance, which pays medical bills

questions.intro: Each insurance covers a different loss: health insurance pays for medical care; life insurance pays beneficiaries at death; disability insurance pays a share of income, often about 60%, while you cannot work. Government disability benefits have strict rules and waiting periods.
sources: NAIC (Consumer insurance guides): Explains auto, home, renters, life, and disability insurance and how deductibles affect premiums. (https://content.naic.org/consumer)

Social Security Administration (Disability benefits): Social Security disability benefits have strict eligibility rules and a waiting period, so many workers also rely on private or employer disability insurance. (https://www.ssa.gov/disability)

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between term and whole life insurance?

choices.text: Term covers only accidents; whole life covers only illness
Term is for children; whole life is for adults
Term covers a set period; whole life lasts for life
Term pays while you live; whole life pays at death

questions.correct_answer: Term covers a set period; whole life lasts for life
questions.intro: Life insurance pays a death benefit to beneficiaries. Term life covers a set number of years and is much cheaper. Whole (permanent) life lasts for life and includes a cash value, with much higher premiums.
questions.feedback: Term is temporary and cheaper; whole life is permanent with cash value.

choices.text: A teenager with no dependents and no debts
A retiree whose savings cover the spouse's needs
A single adult whose only bills are their own
A parent whose income supports young children

questions.correct_answer: A parent whose income supports young children
questions.intro: Life insurance protects people who depend on your income. A common estimate is several times yearly income, adjusted for debts and savings.
questions.feedback: Life insurance matters most when others depend on your income.

questions.prompt: What does homeowners insurance usually cover that renters insurance does not?

choices.text: The building itself
Personal belongings such as a laptop
Liability if a guest is hurt
Living costs after a covered loss

questions.intro: Renters insurance covers belongings and liability; the landlord insures the building. Homeowners insurance also covers the structure. Lenders require it for a mortgage.
questions.feedback: Homeowners insurance adds coverage for the dwelling.

questions.intro: Rules of thumb are a starting point. A needs-based estimate adds debts, future costs such as college, and years of income, then subtracts savings.

questions.prompt: A disability policy has a 90-day elimination period. What does that mean?

choices.text: The policy ends after 90 days
Benefits start after 90 days of disability
Claims must be filed within 90 minutes of an injury
The premium is free for 90 days

questions.correct_answer: Benefits start after 90 days of disability
questions.intro: The elimination (waiting) period is how long you must be disabled before benefits begin. An emergency fund covers that gap.
questions.feedback: Benefits begin after the waiting period.

choices.text: Workplace plans always replace 100% of income
Government benefits are automatic and immediate

To replace more income

questions.feedback: Extra coverage can fill gaps in employer benefits.
